nota: Archived NASA data, downloaded on 2026-11-14. Daily dose = mean of hourly absorbed_dose_rate from LRO/CRaTER-D1D2 (lunar orbit). Calm reference: 5.0 µGy/h (May 5, 2024). Level = day mean / calm: below 1.6 = 0, below 10 = 1, below 100 = 2, otherwise 3. Forecast range: made by the game from the DONKI events known that morning (flares, CMEs, particles, ENLIL runs); it is not an official NASA forecast.
instrumento: the CRaTER instrument on NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), in orbit around the Moon

fontes.nome: LRO / CRaTER radiation dose, via NASA OSDR RadLab

dias.curto: A flare flashed on the Sun.
dias.aviso: Good morning, Commander! At 06:01 UTC the Sun fired an X1.3 flare from sunspot region 13663. A flare is a flash of light and X-rays.
dias.fato: Flares are ranked A, B, C, M and X. X is the strongest. Light from the Sun reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes.

dias.curto: A big X4.5 flare on the Sun!
dias.aviso: Big flash! An X4.5 flare at 06:35 UTC.
dias.fato: Sunspots are darker, cooler areas on the Sun with strong magnetic fields. Most big flares start there.

dias.aviso: A quieter day: only M-class flares (M5.1 and M8.2).
dias.fato: The Moon has no thick air and no global magnetic field. On Earth, both help block radiation from space.

dias.curto: The Sun threw a fast cloud of particles (a CME)!
dias.aviso: Watch out: three X1.0 flares today. At 22:24 UTC the Sun threw a cloud of solar material into space at 1,257 km/s. It is called a CME.
dias.fato: A CME (coronal mass ejection) is a giant cloud of gas and magnetic field thrown out by the Sun. It crosses to the Moon in one to three days.

dias.curto: NASA detected fast particles from the Sun!
dias.aviso: Storm alert! An X2.2 flare at 09:13 UTC. At 13:59 UTC NASA detected fast particles from the Sun.
dias.fato: Solar energetic particles are very fast protons. Thin walls do not stop them, so a base needs radiation shielding.

dias.curto: An X3.9 flare and more fast particles!
dias.aviso: Storm alert! An X3.9 flare at 06:54 UTC and more fast particles from 12:59 UTC. On Earth, a Kp 9 geomagnetic storm starts at 15:00 UTC, the strongest in more than 20 years.
dias.fato: On Earth this storm made auroras far from the poles. Earth's magnetic field protected people there. The Moon has no such shield.

dias.aviso: A giant X5.8 flare at 01:23 UTC. Get the shield ready!
dias.fato: µGy/h (micrograys per hour) measures how much radiation energy a body absorbs each hour.

dias.curto: The flares are getting smaller. Launch tonight!
dias.aviso: The flares are getting smaller. Today is launch day: the rocket must be ready tonight!
dias.fato: NASA's Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office watches the Sun every day and logs events in DONKI, the database this game uses.
